name: Elbow (example)
_UNITS: Every physical value may be written three ways:
3. bare number       "distance_joint_axis_to_CG": 0.28   -> canonical SI assumed, and
flagged in the report's UNIT AUDIT
A unit from the wrong dimension (e.g. kg for a length) is always a hard error.
Set "strict_units": true below to reject form 3 outright.
Canonical units: mass kg, length m, inertia kg.m^2, angle rad, time s,
EXCEPT joint angles (stroke_start, stroke_end, gravity_angle), where a bare
number is read as DEGREES -- nobody writes 90 meaning 90 radians.
torque N.m, angular velocity rad/s, temperature degC.
_comment: Two actuators share one joint: torque and mass scale by n, and each unit carries 1/n of the load so each one's thermal problem gets easier. Set ratio if there is a belt or linkage between the actuator output and the joint itself.

ratio.note: actuators mounted coaxially on the joint, no extra reduction

total_mass_at_CG.note: whole moving assembly: link, bracket, hardware and anything carried

distance_joint_axis_to_CG.note: joint axis to the CG. Counts linearly for gravity and SQUARED for inertia

moment_of_inertia_around_CG.note: about the CG, NOT about the joint axis -- the parallel-axis transfer m*d^2 is added for you. Take this straight from CAD

joint_plane_tilt.note: side-side tilt of the plane (perpendicular to rotation axis) of this joint relative to gravity. 0 = plane is vertical so gravity acts fully; 90 = plane is horizontal (axis vertical) so gravity never loads the joint

gravity_angle.note: joint angle at which the CG points straight DOWN, along the gravity vector. Torque is zero there and peaks 90 deg away. Same frame as profile.stroke_start

stroke_start.note: joint angle at one end of the travel, same frame as load.gravity_angle

stroke_end.note: the other end. The move runs start -> end -> start, repeating

max_velocity.note: joint speed ceiling enforced by the motion controller. If the stroke is long enough to reach it, the move is 'velocity-limited' and gets a constant-speed Cruise phase

max_accel.note: acceleration ceiling. This is KINEMATIC, not a torque limit: the torque needed to achieve it is J_total*max_accel and is computed for you, which is exactly what the Trajectory following check tests

max_jerk.note: rate of change of acceleration, so the S-curve has no instantaneous torque steps. Lower = gentler on the drivetrain but a slower move; a short stroke may be 'jerk-limited', never reaching max_accel at all

dwell_time.note: rest at each end, after arriving and before the return. Shown as Dwell on chart 1. Speed is zero but a gravity-loaded joint still draws holding current, so this is rest, not free. Full cycle = 2*(solved move_time + dwell_time)

profile._solved_note: There is deliberately NO move_time or accel_fraction here. The trajectory is the fastest move that respects all three limits above, so the move time is SOLVED and reported (see COMMANDED MOTION in the report) rather than prescribed. The move is always bound by at least one limit; the report names which. Chart 1 legend: Move_*_Accel / Cruise / Move_*_Decel / Dwell.
profile._samples_note: Resolution of the time discretisation, per traverse. Higher = more, finer segments, so more dots on chart 1 and a slightly more accurate RMS -- but it does NOT change the motion. Floor of 28; 160 is plenty. Dwell stays at 2 points however high this goes, because a dwell is one constant segment per end.

_POWER_SYSTEM: Bus voltage is a property of THIS robot, not of the actuator. The vendor's
rated voltage is only what they characterised the unit at. Set the voltage
your robot actually supplies here; the actuator file declares the range it
will accept, and the two are checked against each other.
Running ABOVE the vendor nominal is routine and simply extends the speed
envelope. Running above their stated MAXIMUM is limited by transistor and
DC-link capacitor voltage ratings rather than by heat, so it cannot be
cleared on thermal grounds; set accept_overvoltage to acknowledge the risk
and downgrade that check from a failure to a warning.
supply_current_limit is optional - omit it if the supply can always deliver
more than the drive's own current rating, which is the usual case.

bus_voltage.note: 13S lithium pack, nominal 48.1 V, 54.6 V at full charge

T_ambient.note: inside the arm shell, NOT room temperature

max_surface_temp.note: housing is reachable by the operator. ISO 13732-1 is the relevant standard for touch-temperature limits; the threshold depends on material and contact duration, so set this from your own safety case rather than treating 48 as a default.
